title: Trace Harvest — weekly notes and standup log (Oct 2 2028)
content:
Week: 2028-10-01 -> 2028-10-07
Owners: Maya (notes), Evan (dashboards), Priya (sampling experiments)
Slack: #obs-trace, #obs-cost, #prod-sre

Summary (one line): Focused week on pruning high-cardinality spans for cost reduction, finished first pass of the low-cost dashboard quilt, and started the adaptive sampler beta on canary traffic.

Morning standups (high level)
- Mon 10/01: Kickoff — align on span bucketing change (BETA) and dashboard quilt layout. Priya to run sample budget sim; Evan to prototype golden-row visualization for top 10 latency contributors.
- Tue 10/02: Discovery — found 3 high-cardinality tags in router spans (country_code, user_agent_version, feature_flag). Decision: drop/rollup by rule, keep one raw tag for rollback debug.
- Wed 10/03: Implementation sync — Samir landed the rollup transform in the ingest pipeline (staging). End-to-end trace still reproducing occasional KV-cache misses.
- Thu 10/04: Canary day — adaptive sampler on 0.5% of production traffic for 12 hours. Observed 22% drop in span volume for the canary group with <1% change in error budgets.
- Fri 10/05: Retro and next steps — agreed to increase canary to 2% next week and run span replay for alerting regression tests.

Key decisions and rationale
- Rollup vs drop: We will rollup user_agent_version to major-version only (e.g., 1.x, 2.x) rather than drop, because telemetry shows a small set of major versions produce most errors and we want signal for targeted patches.
- Adaptive sampler beta: Move forward with budgeted adaptive sampler (controller in python) tied to span-cost budget per service. Rationale: immediate cost wins, maintains tail SLOs in early tests.

Work items and owners (short-term)
- Priya: complete sample-budget simulation spreadsheet and add cost projection for next 30/90/365 days (JIRA-OBS-1218). Due 2028-10-10.
- Evan: finalize dashboard quilt (golden-row + top contributors) and wire to alerting. Draft PR: GH-PR-7192. Due 2028-10-09.
- Samir: iterate on ingest rollup transform to emit a rollup tag and preserve raw in a separate archive stream (staging -> perf tests). Due 2028-10-08.
- Maya: run span-replay harness for canary alerts and add regression tests to tracing-runbook-v2. Due 2028-10-12.

Observations / experiment notes (detailed)
- Adaptive sampler (canary):
  * config: budget=0.5% traffic, min-preserve=5% for error and auth spans, target reduction=20–30% span volume.
  * results: overall span ingestion reduced by 22% in canary window; cost estimate reduction ~18% when extrapolating to full service scale.
  * tail latency: 99.9th stayed within 1.5 ms of baseline for traces that were preserved; some synthetic load test showed small variance under microburst.
  * things to watch: preservation heuristics currently rely on presence of error tag; missing error detection for some services — add sampling exemption for 'auth' and 'payment' service classes.

- Rollup transform for high-cardinality tags:
  * Implementation: Samir added a transform that maps full user_agent_version -> major version and drops raw to archive stream. Country_code previously string with rare values — we will map rare iso codes to 'other' bucket.
  * Risk: Losing fine-grained tag can complicate root-cause when a new user-agent emerges. Mitigation: keep raw archives for 30 days; build quick-restore path (toggle) in the ingest config.

Dashboards and alerts
- Dashboard quilt: Evan prototyped a 'golden-row' that shows per-service cost, span-rate, 99/99.9/avg latency, and sample-rate in one row. This replaces the old multi-panel scatter that was too noisy for on-call.
- New alerts: 'span-cost drift' (alert if ingestion cost rises >10% vs baseline over 24h), 'sample-rate drop' (if sampling controller drops below configured min-preserve).
- Action: Push golden-row to ops dashboard namespace and epoch-rollover to 30-day windows. Need on-call signoff before promoting to main page.

Cost telemetry notes
- Current quarter: traced ingestion costs trending +14% QoQ due to two steady microservices increasing span cardinality after a feature rollout.
- Forecast: With rollups + adaptive sampling at 50% adoption, forecasted reduction of ~32% ingestion cost for traced pipeline in 90 days. This was modeled in Priya's spreadsheet.
- Billing/chargeback: Recommend we tag top 10 deployers with their cost centers and run a biweekly chargeback report for infra-finance visibility.

Open risks and questions (explicit)
- Will rollups hurt anomaly detection that relies on precise tags? (Priya to prototype anomaly detection on rollup test dataset).
- Can we guarantee the archive stream will restore raw tags within the 30 day window without disrupting live ingest? (Samir + infra to validate).
- Do we need a separate SLO for the sampling controller (controller availability affects observability)? Proposed SLO: 99.95% for controller reconciliation loops.

Meeting artifacts and links
- Recording: https://meet.redwood.ai/obs/trace-harvest-2028-10-02
- Slides: confluence:tracing-weekly-2028-10-02/slides
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7192 (dashboard quilt)
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-1218 (sampling sims), JIRA-OBS-1220 (ingest rollup), JIRA-OBS-1223 (golden-row promote)

Retro notes (what went well / what didn't)
- Went well: parallel workstreams (sampling + rollup + dashboard) stayed decoupled and we had measurable metrics within 48 hours of canary.
- Pain points: archive toggle path is still manual; engineers spent extra time reconstructing a missing raw tag in staging. Need a playbook for toggle restores.

Next week's goals (prioritized)
1) Increase adaptive sampler canary to 2% traffic, longer window (48h) and validate alert fidelity. Owner: Priya.
2) Finish automatic archive-restore playbook (scripted rollback). Owner: Samir + infra lead.
3) Promote golden-row to on-call dashboard after one more dry-run. Owner: Evan + SRE.
4) Start a short pilot with infra-finance for cost chargeback for top 10 services. Owner: Maya + finance-rep.

Notes to self (fragments / rough ideas)
- Consider an internal dashboard showing 'span-density' heatmap (span keys x unique values) so product teams can see what tags explode after rollouts.
- Long-term: move sampling controller from python prototype -> rust operator for lower latency and resource usage.
- Keep an eye on cold-path archival costs — cheap storage spike if we keep raw traces for 90+ days.

End of notes.

Unresolved edits: need to attach Priya's simulation CSV and Evan's mockup PNG before finalizing.
